title: Australia | WHS, the Positive Duty and Whistleblower Protections in Banking
tagline: Keep people safe, prevent harassment and protect those who speak up: the Australian laws behind a bank's people-safety duties.
sectors: People and culture, safety and wellbeing teams
description:
This quest teaches the Australian laws that shape how a bank protects its people. It covers the **primary duty of care** in the **Work Health and Safety Act 2011** (s 19, including the duty in s 19(3)(f) to provide the information, training, instruction or supervision needed to protect people), officers' due diligence, consultation, health and safety representatives and psychosocial hazards; the **positive duty** in **s 47C of the Sex Discrimination Act 1984** and the **Australian Human Rights Commission's** powers to enforce it; the whistleblower protections in **Part 9.4AAA of the Corporations Act 2001**, as overseen by **ASIC**; and, in general terms, the **Financial Accountability Regime** administered by **APRA** and ASIC.

It is for all bank staff, people managers, health and safety representatives, eligible recipients of whistleblower disclosures and accountable executives: the WHS Act requires the training workers need to be protected, and ASIC and the Commission expect people to know how to prevent harassment and handle disclosures.

You follow a fictional team at Tasman Ridge Bank in Sydney, Parramatta and Hobart, and study real APRA and ASIC cases.

This quest builds knowledge of the law and good practice; it does not replace your institution's own policies, procedures or advice from your safety, people or compliance teams.
audience: All bank employees, including contact centre and branch staff
Health and safety representatives and people and culture teams
Whistleblower protection officers, eligible recipients and investigators
Senior executives, FAR accountable persons and directors
outcomes: Apply the WHS primary duty, including the duty to provide necessary information, training, instruction and supervision
Identify and control psychosocial hazards and consult workers and HSRs on changes that affect their safety
Explain and apply the Sex Discrimination Act positive duty to harassment by colleagues and customers
Decide whether a whistleblower disclosure is protected and handle it with confidentiality and without detriment
Describe FAR accountability obligations and how they connect to people-safety oversight
Assemble evidence of a working people-safety and speak-up program for boards and regulators

quest.name: The Safe Voice Mission
quest.premise: You have joined the people risk and safety team at Tasman Ridge Bank in Sydney. With safety head Leila Nasser, HSR Ben Tran, whistleblower protection officer Aroha Ngata, COO James Whitfield and Hobart branch manager Chloe Papadopoulos, you must make sure every worker is safe, free from harassment and protected when they speak up, and that someone is accountable for it all.
